tasks.short: Develop the script and the story board.

steps.what: Draft pre-production outlines from the assignment specifications.

loop.purpose: Bind each heading to a field in the assignment specification.
loop.output: Pre-production outlines whose headings cite those fields.
loop.check: Each heading cites a specification field id.
loop.stop: No field id, or the heading is not asked for in the specification.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed heading list cannot tell which heading the assignment specification did not ask for.

steps.what: Develop scripts, story boards, and graphics using own ideas or the specifications.
File the accepted script, story board, and graphics.

tasks.design: A draft in {DOCS} builds pre-production outlines only from fields in the assignment specification, and it stops on a heading the specification did not ask for. The audio technician develops the script, the story board, and the graphics, using the technician's own ideas or those specifications. The accepted version is filed only after that work. The outline is not the script. An assignment with no specification is not drafted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The brief was a mail, and the outline, the script, and the story board were separate files with no shared headings.
tasks.enabler_now: Headings can be drafted from specification fields. The script and the story board are still written by the technician.
tasks.still_hard: What the piece should say, and which idea is the technician's own, is not in the specification.
tasks.human_edge: The technician develops the script and the story board. The outline only repeats headings the specification already contains.
tasks.altitude: The technician still writes the script, the story board, and the graphics. An outline is filed only after the technician accepts that version.

reach.task: Draft from a brief and still write the piece.
reach.learn: A heading taken from the brief is not the piece.

evidence.claim: An outline can repeat headings that already appear as fields in an assignment specification. It cannot supply the script, the story board, or the technician's own ideas.
Filing is a copy of the version the technician accepted. The draft outline is not that version.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The assignment id and the specification field ids. A heading with no field id is not drafted. Ideas that are not in the specification are written by the technician, not by the draft. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the specification from the document store already used for the assignment before adding a new brief.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the audio technician.
unknowns: Whether story boards are drawn by this technician or by a designer.
research_questions: Who accepts the script before it may be filed, the technician or the director?

already_counted.description: Developing the script, the story board, and the graphics stays with the technician.

incremental.description: Drop outlines for assignments that were withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: script version and the specification field ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still develops the script, the story board, and the graphics, and still accepts the version that is filed. The draft removes only headings already present as specification fields. An assignment with no specification saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List license and warranty information stored for the audio and video facilities.
Maintain compliance information by checking the related license paper.
Organize the accepted license and warranty information.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store lists license and warranty dates already stored for the audio and video facilities. The audio technician checks the paper for compliance information the register does not hold, and maintains the record only after that check. The accepted information is organized into the register for that version. A blank expiry is not listed and is not invented. The date does not decide whether the licence covers the use. No reminder is treated as labour the technician used to spend unless the technician was the one sending it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Licences sat in a folder, and an expiry was noticed when a shoot was already booked.
tasks.enabler_now: Dates already stored can be listed. Deciding what an unseen licence covers still takes the paper and the technician.
tasks.still_hard: A date does not say whether the licence allows this facility, this event, or this copy.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks the licence paper. The list only shows dates the register already holds.

ambition.what: Look at each stored licence expiry in the week it falls due, before a facility is booked for that week.

tasks.altitude: The technician still reads any licence the register does not hold. Expiry dates already stored are listed in the week they fall due, and only an accepted record is filed.

reach.task: Keep the licence beside the work it covers.
reach.learn: An expiry date is not a reading of the licence.

evidence.claim: A register can list expiry dates already stored and can be configured with a reminder. The list does not decide whether a licence covers the use.
Checking the paper is the technician's reading. Filing stores only the information the technician has accepted, and a reminder the register sends is not hours the technician spends.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The facility id and the expiry date only if it is already stored. A blank date is not listed and is not guessed. The licence paper is the source for anything the register lacks. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Configure the document store the company already keeps licences in before building a separate register.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the audio technician.
A reminder sent by the register is system runtime and is outside these shares.
unknowns: Whether licences are held by facilities staff rather than by the technician.
research_questions: Which licence types must be read in full, rather than listed by expiry only?

already_counted.description: Checking the licence paper stays with the technician.

incremental.description: Remove licence rows for facilities the company no longer runs.

approvals.approved_version: license version and the facility id it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still checks any licence the register does not hold, and still accepts the record before it is filed. Listing dates already stored is the removed time. A reminder the register sends is not counted, because that is not the technician's labour. A blank date saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the approved audio and videotaping service policy.
Inform users of audio and videotaping policies and procedures.
Note a question the approved policy text does not answer.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the audio and videotaping service policy if it is already approved. The audio technician informs the user of the policies and procedures in conversation. A question the text does not answer is noted by the technician and is not answered from guesswork. The screen does not inform the user. A missing policy leaves the screen blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: The policy was a page on the intranet, and users were told it from memory at the booking.
tasks.enabler_now: The approved policy can be open during the conversation. Informing the user still takes the technician.
tasks.still_hard: A user question about their own event is often not answered by the policy text.
tasks.human_edge: The technician informs the user and notices when the policy does not answer the question.
tasks.altitude: The conversation stays with the technician. The approved policy is visible, and an unanswered question is noted rather than filled in.

reach.task: Explain a rule to a person and admit when the rule is silent.
reach.learn: The rule text is not the explanation.

evidence.claim: Showing a policy that is already approved is a lookup. It does not inform the user.
An unanswered question is noted by the technician. Inventing a procedure the policy does not state would misstate the rule.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The policy id and the policy text only if it is already approved. The text is not drafted here. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the policy from the document store before copying it into a mail.
unknowns: Whether users are staff or external bookers of the videotaping service.
research_questions: Who approves a change to the videotaping policy?

already_counted.description: Informing the user and noting an unanswered question stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Replace the shown policy when an approved revision is published.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still informs the user of the policy in conversation and still notes a question the text does not answer. Only showing a policy that is already approved is removed. A missing policy saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Total the audio-visual activity counts already stored in the log.
Analyze the audio-visual activity log and decide what it means.
Maintain the written conclusion beside the activity log.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store totals activity counts already stored in the audio-visual log. The audio technician analyzes the log and decides what the totals mean, then writes that conclusion. The total is arithmetic on stored counts. It is not the analysis. A log with no counts is not totalled. The conclusion is the technician's, and it is not generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were added by hand from a sheet, and the conclusion was a sentence in a mail that did not cite the sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored counts can be totalled. Saying what the week means stays with the technician.
tasks.still_hard: A higher count can be a busier week or a change in how activities are logged, and the total cannot say which.
tasks.human_edge: The technician decides what the log means and writes the conclusion.
tasks.altitude: The conclusion stays with the technician. Totals are arithmetic on counts already in the log, and they are not treated as the analysis.

reach.task: Read a count of jobs and still say what it means for the work.
reach.learn: A total is not the conclusion.

evidence.claim: Adding counts already stored in a log is arithmetic. It does not analyze the activities or decide what they mean.
The conclusion is written by the technician. A total does not contain it, and no report is generated from the total alone.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The log id and the activity counts already stored. A missing count is not treated as zero. The total does not classify an activity. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Total the log in the document store already used for it before exporting to a new report.
unknowns: Whether activities are logged by this technician or by the people who book the rooms.
research_questions: Which activity types are in the log, and which are kept elsewhere?

already_counted.description: Analyzing the log and writing the conclusion stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Correct a stored count when an activity was logged twice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still analyzes the log and still writes the conclusion. Only totalling counts already stored is removed. A log with missing counts is not filled with zeros, so that week saves nothing of the analysis.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician still writes the script and the story board, still checks a licence the register does not hold, still tells the user the policy, and still says what the log means. Drafts and totals are not those decisions.
reach: Poets, lyricists and creative writers draft from a brief, and this job learns the assignment is not the script.
Art directors keep a licence with a work, and this job learns an expiry date is not a reading of the licence.
skills_to_grow: Edit the script and the story board after any outline drafted from the assignment.
Check a licence the register does not already hold before it is filed.
Read a log total as arithmetic, and keep the conclusion.
role.ambitious_version: Scripts, licence judgements, policy conversations, and log conclusions stay with the technician. A filed licence is only the one the technician has accepted.
